phase_dictionary — DRIVE pxrd op

• Data kinds: any × signal × scalar → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.phase_dictionary(phases, two_theta, wavelength, size=inf, K=0.9, instrumental_fwhm=0.02, lorentz='powder', eta=0.0) (to call the implementation directly, import pxrd; pxrd.phase_dictionary(phases, two_theta, wavelength, size=inf, K=0.9, instrumental_fwhm=0.02, lorentz='powder', eta=0.0); from the registry, opsdrive.get("phase_dictionary"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Dictionary of phase reference patterns: on a 2θ grid, the 1-D intensity per volume fraction of 1 is arranged for each phase.

1 row = (1/V²) Σ m|F|² L(2θ) × 形 (the shape is a pseudo-Voigt whose width is the Gaussian sum of the Scherrer size [Å] and the instrument FWHM; eta is the Lorentz fraction). instrumental_fwhm is a number [deg] or a table (2θ の列, FWHM の列) —— on a flat detector the angle subtended by a pixel shrinks as cos² 2θ, so the instrumental width changes with 2θ. The proper approach is to integrate an image of a standard without broadening (Si) in the same geometry and pass the FWHM from diffraction_peaks as the table (the PoC procedure). This matches the same quantity as a profile from azimuthal_integrate run with polarisation and solid-angle corrections. If the width does not match, the NNLS scale factors are biased —— the proper approach is to estimate size first with the FWHM from diffraction_peaks and scherrer_size.

Return value (dict): names, two_theta, matrix ((P, n)), density [g/cm³], phases (the original phases, for redrawing during lattice refinement), params (wavelength, width, Lorentz).

Raises ValueError: phases empty or not in phase form, duplicate names, lattice does not increase, invalid width values.
